html:
Killing of Ii Naosuke, the chief minister of the shogun, by a band of samurai outside the Sakuradamon gate of Edo Castle, in snow, on 24 March 1860.

Ii had signed trade treaties with the United States and other powers in 1858 without the emperor's consent, following Perry's opening of Japan. He then jailed or executed critics in the Ansei Purge. Eighteen men, most from Mito domain with one from Satsuma, ambushed his procession and cut off his head.

The murder showed that the shogunate could not protect even its top official in its own capital. The shogunate's authority shrank, and more political killings followed, especially in Kyoto. The government there turned to the Shinsengumi to keep order. The road led on to the Meiji Restoration in 1868.
